summary: Pulaski County tower site listed at 302 ft with no build record. A 2013 FFLA report said a Pulaski County tower would be auctioned for removal, unnamed; OSM maps a lattice tower.

events.note: FFLA chapter report, secondhand: a Pulaski County tower was to be auctioned for removal. The report does not name the tower or confirm a sale.

evidence.supports: tower list gives the Pulaski Lookout Tower coordinates, a 302-foot elevation and the numbers BLL-64710 and gfc-335
OpenStreetMap has a point named Pulaski Lookout Tower
the point is tagged as an observation tower
the point is tagged with lattice construction
the author understood that a Pulaski County tower would be auctioned for removal
evidence.quote: I understand that 2 towers will be coming up for auction for removal

evidence.supports: the Pulaski County tower is the second of two towers named in the report
the first of the two towers is in Richmond County, near Augusta
evidence.quote: Richmond County, which is near Augusta

evidence.supports: the report's author was the Georgia and South Carolina area representative

sources.title: Georgia/South Carolina Chapter Representative Report for 2013

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The tower list gives coordinates, a 302-ft elevation and the numbers BLL-64710 and gfc-335. The OSM point is tagged as a lattice observation tower, with no history. The only history is the 2013 FFLA report, which is secondhand and does not name the tower; the report concerns a tower 'in Pulaski County', which may or may not be this site. Forest Lookouts' Pulaski page gives only the name and county. Two web searches found no Pulaski tower history. A 2024 Hawkinsville survey describes a proposed Verizon cell tower called the Pulaski Tower; it is not a lookout and is not used. The brief's status 'unknown' is kept.
